review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. Pacific catch-rate and satellite-tag studies support 20-25 °C habitat, while vertical depth is not seafloor bathymetry.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 1 per harvester / day
profile.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, squids, and pelagic prey
profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for striped marlin.
factors.value_notes: North Pacific research reports 20-25 °C as a preferred temperature range; California/Mexico recreational catch rates were highest around 22-24 °C, and longline analyses report 20-26 °C. These align well with the configured 18-26 °C range and 20-24 °C ideal. However, habitat is non-contiguous and stock/region/season effects are substantial, so this is not a universal global catch curve.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for striped marlin.
factors.value_notes: Satellite tags show striped marlin spend much of their time near the surface but can dive to 460 m or deeper depending on oxygen, thermocline and region. The runtime variable is seafloor bathymetry, not fish vertical depth; the configured 0-100 m seabed band is only a weak shelf/offshore proxy.

text.day: Full daylight when Pacific gamefish actively hunt.
